newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues rules on futures trading accounting.
newsitem.headline: China issues rules on futures trading accounting.

text.p: China on Wednesday issued a set of rules governing accounting of commodity futures trading, focusing on risk control and requiring exchanges to put aside 20 percent of their commission income as risk-control funds.
The rules, published in the China Securities newspaper and with immediate effect, also require futures brokerages to put aside five percent of their income to cover possible losses.
"The rules aim to standardise accounting of futures trading, ensure healthy development of commodity futures markets and protect the interests of the state and of investors," the newspaper said.
According to the rules, futures exchanges must ensure that every member has one independent account for futures trading. Exchanges themselves must not trade.
Members must pay enough margin requirements before they can trade futures and there must be checks on the margins at the end of each day's trading to ensure the provision is abided by.
Futures brokerages must ask customers to pay enough margin requirements for futures trading and check their accounts at the end of each trading day to ensure this is done.
They must not use irregular means, including discounts, to attract customers.
Under the new rules, companies trading on the futures markets must have independent trading accounts, and traders and accountants must be strictly separated.
Those firms which have made losses for three successive years and are on the brink of bankruptcy will be banned from futures trading, according to the rules.
State companies must not borrow from other firms or financial institutions to trade futures, the rules said.
